keyTerms.note: A verb of lowering and giving way, used of ground that sinks underfoot. Applied to speech it names a pliancy of tone rather than the volume of a voice or the content of what is said.
A verb for wanting what one has no claim to. The clause places the difficulty in a particular hearer's appetite, which is why the ayah goes on to bound the manner rather than require silence.
From the verb to know, so it means speech of a kind everybody recognises as proper. The word runs through the Quran for conduct a community can identify without any rule being stated.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Households in the city were not sealed off from the street. Doorways opened onto lanes, courtyards were shared between families, and a woman answering a caller at her door was entirely ordinary. Reputation in a settlement of a few thousand travelled by exactly such small encounters, remembered and repeated. The instruction here concerns how a routine exchange sounded, in a place where everyone heard everything.
studies.didYouKnow: The clause about the one with sickness in his heart uses a phrase that occurs about a dozen times in the Quran, twice in this surah alone. In every other place it describes people in a political situation, wavering under pressure. Only here is it attached to appetite, and the classical commentators discuss the extension as a reach of the same underlying condition.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Distinction is made conditional on conduct, so standing is not treated as a possession that holds by itself. The instruction is also split into a limit and a requirement, and the requirement is the larger of the two: speech is called for, and only its manner is bounded. Naming the hearer's disorder rather than the speaker's intention places responsibility carefully, in a way later readers can apply in either direction.

crossReferences.why: Addresses restraint to men and to women in turn, beginning with the men.
Belongs to the same sequence about the household and turns on a comparable boundary.
Uses the same word for speech recognised as right, in a completely different setting.

studies.applyIt: Notice that this ayah does not ask for less speech, only for a different register. Pick one conversation this week where you usually adjust your tone to manage how the other person feels about you. Say the same thing in a plain register instead. The content need not change at all; the ayah is interested in what the tone is doing.

studies.title: The Household And Its Purity
studies.meaning: Five instructions are given to the household, and then the ayah turns without warning into a statement about what God intends. The grammatical form of the address shifts in that last clause, and the classical commentators divide over its reference. Some read the People of the Household as the wives, since the entire passage addresses them. Some read it as taking in the closest kin. Some read it as both together. The tradition records these readings alongside one another.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, in the passage addressed to the household after the choice offered a few ayat earlier. The reference to a former age of ignorance points back to customs of display before the change, which the commentators describe in general terms rather than in detail. The final clause has been discussed at length in the classical literature, and the divergence over whom it names is old and is reported by the major commentators without rancour.

keyTerms.note: Built from the word for a tower, so it means to make something conspicuous by raising it where it will be seen. The image behind the verb is architectural before it is personal.

A noun for the period before the revelation, from the root for not knowing. It occurs four times in the Quran, and here it is qualified as the former one, which the commentators read in more than one way.
A word for what repels, covering physical filth and moral corruption together. It is named as the thing being removed, and the sentence supplies no list of what falls under it.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Display was a public language in that society. A woman of standing signalled her family's position by what she wore and by how she moved through a market or a gathering, and the signalling was expected of her rather than indulged. Customs varied between the towns and the tribes, and the commentators describe the older practice generally. What this ayah addresses is a way of being seen, where being seen was itself a statement.
studies.didYouKnow: The word for the age before the revelation occurs four times in the Quran. Once it names a kind of thinking, once a kind of judgement, once a heated partisanship, and here a kind of display. The classical commentators observe that the Quran never uses the term for a period on its own; it always attaches it to something specific that the period produced.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The ayah moves from instructions to an intention, and the intention belongs to God rather than to the people addressed. That reframes everything before it: the instructions are described as serving a purpose being carried out on them, not merely required of them. The divergence over exactly whom the final clause names is long-standing in the tradition, and the passage is read with reverence for the whole household on every side of it.

crossReferences.why: Opens the same address and states the distinction this ayah then builds upon.
Closes the sequence by pointing at what is recited inside these same homes.
Uses the same word for display in a general setting, so it is not confined here.

studies.applyIt: Notice that the last clause of this ayah is about what God intends rather than about what anyone is asked to do. Take one habit you keep for its own sake, a prayer, a silence, an early hour. Hold it this week as something being done to you rather than by you, and see whether that makes it lighter to carry.

studies.title: What Is Recited In Your Homes
studies.meaning: One instruction closes the passage, and it concerns memory rather than conduct: keep in mind what is recited in your houses of God's signs and of wisdom. The two nouns are distinct, and the commentators generally read the second as what accompanies the recitation rather than as another name for it. The two divine names at the end describe a knowledge that reaches into fine and hidden things, and they attach to the whole sequence rather than to this line alone.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, the last ayah of the passage addressed to the household. Revelation arrived in and around these houses across years, and the wisdom named alongside it is generally read as the Prophet's own explanation and practice. The commentators treat the ayah as making the household a place where what came was kept, which was a genuine function in a community whose knowledge was carried in memory rather than on paper.

keyTerms.gloss: keep in mind, call to mind
keyTerms.note: The imperative of a verb that means both remembering inwardly and mentioning aloud. In a society transmitting by recitation those were not two operations but one, which the single word records.
A passive from a verb whose root means to follow. Recitation in this vocabulary is a following of what came before, word after word in order, and the same root gives the word for succession.
A name from a root that joins fineness of texture to gentleness of handling. It describes a knowledge that reaches what is small and concealed without any force involved in the reaching.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Almost nothing was written down. What a community knew, it knew because particular people held it and could produce it when asked, and households were where such holdings accumulated. Children grew up hearing texts repeated at all hours and absorbed them without effort or intention. A house in which revelation was recited daily was, in the plainest practical terms, an archive with a roof over it.
studies.didYouKnow: The two names of God that close this ayah are paired several times in the Quran, and the first of them is rare. Its root supplies the ordinary Arabic words for something fine in texture and for gentleness of manner, so the name carries delicacy of touch alongside delicacy of perception, which the classical commentators discuss at some length.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The passage ends not with an instruction about conduct but with one about attention, which locates this household's real work in what it retained. That gives memory a standing a modern reader is likely to underestimate: in this setting, remembering was the mechanism by which revelation continued to exist. The closing names then attach an ordinary domestic activity to a God described as reaching what is fine and hidden.

crossReferences.why: Pairs signs recited with the teaching of the Book and wisdom in the same construction.
Describes a messenger sent to recite signs, to purify, and to teach the Book and wisdom.
Repeats the same sequence for a people who had held no scripture before it came.

studies.applyIt: Think about what is regularly heard in the room you spend most of your evenings in. Not what you believe, what is audible. This ayah treats the sound of a house as a form of keeping. Put one thing on for ten minutes this week that you would want a child in the next room to absorb without trying.

studies.title: Ten Qualities Named Twice
studies.meaning: Ten qualities are listed, and each is named twice over, once in the masculine and once in the feminine, with no difference in the description and one reward announced at the end for the whole set. The list runs from submission and belief through devotion, truthfulness, patience, humility, giving, fasting, restraint and remembrance. Only the last carries a qualifier, and it is about frequency rather than about degree. Read aloud, the doubling is the most audible feature of the ayah.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan. The classical commentators report an occasion for this ayah on which the sources broadly agree: women of the community asked why the revelation addressed men in its wording and did not mention them, and this ayah followed. The reports differ over which woman put the question and in what setting, but the substance of the account is consistent across them and is given by the major commentaries.

keyTerms.note: From a root meaning to stand in sustained obedience, and used of long standing in prayer. The word carries steadiness over time rather than compliance in a single instance.
Used of ground that has sunk and of a voice dropping. It describes a lowering that happens in the presence of something, not a modest opinion a person holds about themselves.
The only quality in the list given a qualifier, and the qualifier is frequency rather than intensity. It covers both calling to mind and saying aloud, with no line drawn between them.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Women in Medina farmed, traded, held property in their own names and treated the wounded after engagements. Public religious life in Arabia, though, had been male in its forms: the custodians of the sanctuary, the poets who spoke for a tribe, the men who settled disputes in assembly. An address that named both sides in identical terms, ten times in succession, was formally unusual in that setting.
studies.didYouKnow: This is the Quran's most sustained use of paired masculine and feminine forms. The ayah is a single sentence in which each masculine plural is immediately followed by its feminine counterpart, ten times, before the sentence finally reaches its verb and states one reward for all twenty groups at once.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The list is of qualities rather than of roles, and the reward is stated once for the whole of it, which places the same standard on everyone named. It also amounts to a compact account of what the Quran counts as religious life, and the balance is worth noticing: most items are interior states or habits, and only two of the ten would be visible to somebody watching from outside.

crossReferences.why: States the same equality as a principle: no worker's work is lost, male or female, each from the other.
Attaches a good life in this world to the same condition, whoever does good and believes, male or female.
Applies it to the outcome, entry to the Garden granted on the same terms without the smallest reduction.

studies.applyIt: Read the ten qualities slowly and pick the one you would score lowest on, honestly rather than modestly. Then do the smallest possible version of it today: one honest sentence, one held tongue, one thing given away. Ten is a long list, and the point of a long list is that nobody is expected to start at the top of it.

studies.title: No Choice Left In The Matter
studies.meaning: A general rule stated in the negative: once God and His Messenger have settled a matter, no option remains to a believing man or a believing woman about their own affair. The commentators note that both are named, which is deliberate. What is denied is not opinion but the choice that survives a decision, and the closing clause calls the alternative a plain straying. The word used for having a choice occurs only twice in the whole Quran.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, placed immediately before the account of a marriage that ran against a strong social expectation. Commentators connect the ayah to a reported case in which a proposed match was resisted by the family concerned because of a difference in standing. The reports differ over the details, and the commentators treat the general principle rather than the particulars as the settled content of the ayah.

keyTerms.note: A verb for bringing a matter to completion, used of judgements handed down and of work finished. It marks the decision as closed rather than proposed, which is what allows the next clause to follow.
A noun for the freedom to select among alternatives. It occurs only twice in the Quran; the other passage says God creates and chooses, and that they hold no such option themselves.
The noun for wandering off a path, placed after its own verb to intensify it. The word attached to it means plain, so the deviation is described as visible rather than as a subtle error.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Marriage across social lines was the sharpest test of any claim about equality in that society. Families measured a match by lineage as carefully as by property, and a mismatch registered as a loss of standing for everyone connected to it. Resistance in such a case was not stubbornness; it was the ordinary protection of a family's position, which is what makes the flatness of this ayah so pointed.
studies.didYouKnow: The noun used here for having a choice occurs in only one other place in the Quran. There it appears in a statement that God creates whatever He wills and chooses, and that they hold no such choice. Between them the two occurrences give the word its entire range in the Book: one about God's selection, one about where the human option ends.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Faith is defined here partly as the closing of deliberation at a particular point. Deliberation before a decision is nowhere criticised in the Quran, and consultation is repeatedly commended; what this ayah describes is the state of a matter once it is settled. Naming believing men and believing women equally also establishes that the principle addresses a whole community, which the passage immediately following then illustrates in a case.

crossReferences.why: The only other place using this word, saying God chooses and they have no choice.
Makes the same point under an oath, describing believers who feel no resistance inside themselves.
Gives the answer of believers summoned to God and His Messenger for a judgement.

studies.applyIt: Notice how much of your energy goes into reopening decisions that are already made, yours or somebody else's. This ayah is about the specific moment when a matter closes. Pick one settled thing you keep quietly relitigating in your head and let it be closed for a week. See what your attention does with the space it gets back.

studies.title: You Feared The People
studies.meaning: The ayah addresses the Prophet about a conversation, and it is unusually exposing. He had advised a man to keep his wife and to be mindful of God, while holding inside himself something God intended to bring into the open, and the ayah says he feared people when God had the greater right to be feared. Then the marriage that followed is described, with a purpose attached: that no constriction remain for believers over the former wives of adopted sons.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan. The surah opened by denying that adoption makes a son, and this is where that denial is worked through in a case rather than in a rule. The classical accounts describe a marriage between two people close to the household which had come to an end, and the difficulty that followed because the man had once been adopted. The purpose stated inside the ayah is the one the commentators treat as decisive.

keyTerms.note: The imperative of a verb for gripping something and not letting go, and the ordinary term for maintaining a marriage. Its presence records advice given in the opposite direction to what eventually happened.
A verb for hiding rather than for saying anything false. What is at issue is something unspoken, and the severity of the ayah falls on the concealing rather than on any words.
A word for narrowness, a place too tight to move in. The stated purpose of the whole episode is the removal of a constriction, which is how the Quran often describes what a change of practice does.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Adoption had generated a whole set of relations that everyone treated exactly as blood: who could marry whom, who inherited from whom, who was owed protection. Undoing that fiction meant unpicking every one of them, and the most difficult was the relation this ayah addresses. A rule announced in words would have shifted very little where custom ran this deep. What broke it was a case that people could see.
studies.didYouKnow: This ayah contains the only place in the Quran where a man of the Prophet's own community is named. Every other companion appears in the Book unnamed, referred to by description or in the plural. The classical commentators note the singularity and connect it to the function of the passage: the naming is what makes the case unmistakable rather than illustrative.
studies.theologicalSignificance: A prophet is recorded being corrected, in the scripture his own community recites, about a fear of what people would say. That is a remarkable thing for a text to preserve, and it establishes something about prophecy: the messenger is not presented as standing outside ordinary pressure, and the record is not tidied to protect him. It also shows a deep custom being ended by a lived instance rather than by an announcement.

crossReferences.why: States the principle about adopted sons that this ayah then works out in a case.
Answers the difficulty raised here, saying no blame attaches in what God ordained.
Preserves another correction of the Prophet inside the text his community recites.

studies.applyIt: The hardest sentence here is the one about fearing people. Notice one thing you are not saying this week because of how it will land, rather than because it is wrong. You do not have to say it today. Name accurately which of the two fears is holding it back, and let that be the whole exercise.

studies.title: Fearing No One But God
studies.meaning: A general statement follows a particular case: no constriction attaches to the Prophet in what God has assigned him, and this is described as God's established way with those who went before. The word for that way names a track worn by repeated use. Then a relative clause describes the men concerned, and it turns out to be about fear. They deliver God's messages, they fear Him, and they fear nobody else. The last name given presents God as the one keeping the account.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, directly after the case that ended the treatment of adopted sons as sons. The commentators read these two ayat as answering a reaction: the marriage described had cut against a strong social expectation, and there was talk about it in the city. The appeal to the pattern among earlier prophets places the present difficulty inside a long series rather than treating it as something unprecedented.

keyTerms.note: The word for a path worn smooth by repeated use, and by extension a settled practice. Attributed to God it names a consistency in how He deals with people, which is what lets it be cited as evidence.
A verb for having gone by, used of times and of generations alike. It places the earlier prophets in a completed series, which is what makes it possible to read a pattern from them at all.
From the root for counting and calculation. Naming God as the one keeping the account answers the fear of other people's opinion by pointing at whose assessment is actually being recorded.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Reputation was the currency of that world and it was audited constantly. A man's marriages, his generosity and his conduct in a dispute were discussed in every gathering, and the verdict of the town was effectively enforceable. A poet could damage a family's standing with a single composition that people then repeated for years. The suggestion that only one assessment counted rearranged a person's incentives entirely.
studies.didYouKnow: The phrase for God's established way appears in several places in the Quran, and in most of them it is joined to a statement that no change will be found in it. Two of those occurrences fall in this surah. The classical commentators treat the term as the Quran's own word for pattern in history, used of earlier communities and, as here, of earlier prophets.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Fear is treated as a quantity with one legitimate object, and the passage does not ask anyone to feel less of it. It asks where it is pointed. That is a different demand from courage and a more achievable one. Placing prophets in a series also takes the loneliness out of the position: whatever pressure a given moment applies, the passage says the shape of it is old and the outcome is already recorded.

crossReferences.why: Tells the Messenger to deliver what came down and says God will protect him from people.
Uses the same phrase for God's established way and says no change will be found in it.
Asks whether people are more deserving of your fear than God is.

studies.applyIt: Make a list, in your head, of the people whose opinion actually governs what you do. It is usually shorter than you expect and rarely the people you would name if asked. This passage does not tell you to stop caring what anyone thinks. It asks you to know the list, which is a different and more manageable thing.

studies.title: The Seal Of The Prophets
studies.meaning: A denial and a title arrive in one sentence: he is not the father of any of your men, and he is the messenger of God and the seal of the prophets. Commentators read the seal in two connected senses that are both early, the stamp that closes a document and the last item in a sequence, and they generally hold them together rather than choosing. What follows is unexpected. After a statement of that weight, the address turns to the believers and asks for remembrance, frequent, morning and evening.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan. The ayah follows a passage concerning the household of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Arabian custom by which an adopted son took his father's name and stood in a son's place for inheritance and marriage. The surah has already stated that lineage would not be reckoned that way. The denial at the opening of this ayah belongs to that discussion before it turns into a statement about prophecy.

keyTerms.note: The signet pressed into clay to shut a letter. A seal both ends a document and certifies it, which is why the word carries finality and confirmation together rather than one at the expense of the other.
The verbal noun placed after its own verb for emphasis, so the instruction reads as remembering with real remembrance. The added word for abundance then makes frequency part of the request.
The stretch between the sun losing its heat and dusk, not night. Paired with early morning it marks the two ends of the working day rather than the hours when nothing else is happening.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: A seal was ordinary equipment for anyone who sent letters: a ring pressed into soft clay closed the roll and told the recipient who had sent it, and it was the last thing applied before dispatch. Adoption in Arabia transferred name, inheritance and standing. Saying of a man that he was father to none of the men present was therefore a heavy social statement before it was anything else.
studies.didYouKnow: The Prophet's personal name appears only four times in the whole Quran, and this is one of them. Everywhere else he is addressed or described by title: messenger, prophet, the one wrapped in a cloak, the one addressed as you. The name itself is reserved for a handful of statements about who he is and is not.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Two claims are made together: that the line of prophecy is complete, and that what closes it also authenticates what came before. The instruction that follows is the surprising half. Immediately after a statement about revelation ending, what the community is asked for is not a doctrine to defend but a practice to keep twice daily, which places the continuity in remembrance rather than in any line of succession.

crossReferences.why: Uses the name in the same way, to fix that he is a messenger and that messengers have passed before.
States the scope this ayah implies, a message addressed to all people rather than to one community.
Gives the same two-ended instruction about remembering the name of your Lord, morning and evening.

studies.applyIt: Pick one fixed point in your morning and one in your evening, the kettle boiling or the front door closing, and attach a short phrase of remembrance to each. Keep both under ten seconds. The ayah asks for frequency rather than length, and frequency is built on things that were going to happen anyway.

studies.title: He Reaches Out To You
studies.meaning: The verb at the head of this ayah is the one used elsewhere for what a person does towards God, and here God is its subject and people are its object. The commentators are careful with the reversal: when a human being is the subject the word means prayer, and when God is, it means mercy extended and honour conferred. A purpose is then attached, bringing people out of darknesses into light, and a name for God closes it that is specific to the believers.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, in a stretch of the surah that turns from correction to reassurance. The community had come through a siege and its aftermath, and the surah has spent many ayat on failures inside it. These lines change the direction of address entirely. The commentators note the placement rather than any occasion: what follows the exposure of weakness is a description of what God is doing for the same people.

keyTerms.note: The root joins turning towards something to connecting with it. Used of a person it is the word for prayer; used of God the commentators read it as mercy and honour reaching outward rather than any request.
A plural set against a singular light. The Quran keeps this asymmetry every time the pair appears, and the classical commentators read it as saying there are many ways of being lost and one way out.

An intensive form describing a settled quality rather than an occasional act. Here it is qualified as mercy towards the believers specifically, which is unusual, since the name usually stands unrestricted.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Night in that country was genuinely dark. Away from a fire or a lamp the eye had almost nothing to work with, and travel stopped at dusk unless the moon was high. Light was expensive, measured out in oil, and a household's lamp was lit for a purpose and put out afterwards. Being brought out of darkness described a physical relief everyone in the room had felt.
studies.didYouKnow: Everywhere the Quran uses this pairing, darkness is plural and light is singular, without a single exception across the seven or so places it occurs. The classical commentators noticed the pattern and built a reading on it. The grammar of the phrase is doing the same work as its meaning, which is why translators who level it out lose something.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Placing God as the subject of a verb normally directed towards Him rearranges the relationship. The initiative is described as running the other way, and the angels are joined to it, so the movement towards a person is not an exception but a standing condition. Naming the light in the singular then makes guidance a single destination rather than a set of alternatives, which is a claim the surrounding surah keeps assuming.

crossReferences.why: Uses the same movement out of darkness into light and gives the reverse direction as well.
Attaches the same purpose to the revelations sent down, and closes on gentleness and mercy.
Shows the same verb with a human subject, where it plainly means to pray for someone.

studies.applyIt: Notice that this ayah has God moving towards you rather than the other way round. Most people carry a mental picture in which all the traffic runs one direction. Before you next ask God for something, spend one minute listing what has already arrived without being asked for. Then make the request. The order changes how it feels to make it.

studies.title: A Lamp That Gives Light
studies.meaning: A greeting is named first, one word spoken on the day of meeting, and then the address turns and lists five things a messenger was sent as. Four of them are functions, a witness, a bearer of good news, a warner, a caller. The fifth is not a function at all but an object: a lamp that gives light. The commentators note the shift in kind. The first four describe what he does; the last describes what he is in a room.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, in the reassuring stretch that follows the surah's long account of the siege and of failure inside the community. Commentators report no particular occasion for these ayat and read them as a restatement of the mission at a point where it had been under strain, addressed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) directly and overheard by everyone else.

keyTerms.note: From the root for life, so the word for a greeting in Arabic is built on wishing someone continued living. The ordinary daily exchange is the same word used here for what is said on that day.

The word occurs four times in the Quran. Three of them name the sun. This is the only place where it is applied to a person, and the adjective attached means actively giving light rather than merely shining.
One who has seen and can testify, from the vocabulary of a court and of a contract. Placed first in the list, it makes presence and observation the ground of everything else he is sent to do.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: A lamp in that world was a shallow clay dish with a wick and a little oil, and it lit one corner of one room. It did not illuminate a house. People gathered close to it to eat, to mend, to hear a story told. The image is domestic and modest rather than grand, and the light it names is the kind you sit near rather than the kind that fills a sky.
studies.didYouKnow: The word used here for a lamp appears four times in the Quran. In three of those it names the sun, described once as a lamp placed in the sky and once as blazing. This is the only occurrence where the term is applied to a human being, and the commentators note the difference: the sun is a lamp by nature, and this one is described as one that was sent.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The list moves from what a messenger performs to what he is, and the last item cannot be reduced to an activity. A lamp does not persuade anyone; it makes seeing possible and leaves the seeing to others. That describes a mode of prophecy which does not depend on argument, and it sits deliberately beside the four functions rather than replacing them. Both are needed for the account to be complete.

crossReferences.why: Repeats the same three descriptions, witness and bearer of good news and warner, in identical order.
Uses the same word for a lamp, there of the sun set among the heavens.
Describes a light and a clear Book coming from God, guiding out of darkness.

studies.applyIt: Think of someone who has helped you most by their presence rather than by anything they said. This ayah has a word for that and puts it at the end of the list, after all the doing. Sit somewhere near a person like that this week without an agenda for the conversation. Being in the room is the whole of it.

studies.title: Leave Their Injury Alone
studies.meaning: Good news is to be delivered first, and the content of it is left almost unspecified: a great favour, with no detail attached. Then three instructions follow, and the middle one is the unusual member. Do not comply, leave their injury, rely. The verb in the middle means to let something drop rather than to endure it, so what is asked is not the absorbing of an insult but the declining to pick it up. The surah's opening lines return here almost word for word.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan. The surah began with nearly this same instruction and returns to it after forty ayat that describe exactly what the harm consisted of: whispering during a siege, quiet recruitment, sharp speech afterwards. The commentators note the repetition and read the second occurrence as the practical version, issued once the reader knows in detail what is being left alone.

keyTerms.note: The word for an increase beyond what is owed, from a root meaning surplus. Calling the reward a bounty rather than a wage says it exceeds anything the work could have earned.
An imperative for setting a thing down and walking away from it. It is not the verb for enduring something, so what is asked is a refusal to take the injury up rather than strength in carrying it.
A word for hurt that falls short of real damage, covering an insult, a nuisance, or a small harm. Its scale is part of the instruction: what is being set down is not an atrocity.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Insult in that society was a public instrument with consequences. A satire circulated by a poet could reduce a man's standing for a generation, and letting an affront pass was normally read as an inability to answer it. Honour required a reply, and a reply was expected quickly. The instruction here runs directly against the mechanism by which reputation was defended in every town in Arabia.
studies.didYouKnow: This ayah repeats the opening of the surah almost exactly, including the closing clause about God being sufficient as a trustee. Between the two occurrences the surah has described in detail what the opposition actually did. The classical commentators treat the repetition as a frame around the whole account rather than as a second instruction.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Reliance is placed in a series with two other things and given a specific job. It is not offered as consolation for an injury but as the alternative to answering one, which makes it an action rather than a mood. The good news announced first also matters to the order: what makes a slight droppable is not indifference to it but the presence of something the passage calls great, mentioned before the injury is named at all.

crossReferences.why: Opens the surah with almost the same instruction, before any of the harm is described.
Pairs patience over what they say with a withdrawal described as gracious.
Answers the tightening of the chest at what they say with praise rather than reply.

studies.applyIt: Pick one slight from the last month that you are still composing replies to in your head. The verb here is not endure but put down. Try saying to yourself once, plainly, that you are leaving it. Not forgiving it yet, not resolving it. Just declining to carry it around today, and noticing how much attention comes back.

studies.title: Release Them In A Gracious Way
studies.meaning: A narrow case is described, a marriage ended before it has begun in fact, and the counting period that ordinarily follows is said not to apply, since its purpose does not arise. What the ayah then adds is the interesting part. Nothing obliges generosity in a case where nothing was owed, and yet provision and a gracious release are both named. The commentators read the ending as the ayah's point: the reduction of a requirement is not treated as a licence to part badly.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, inside a run of passages about households and their arrangements. Marriage in that society was a contract between families with defined stages, and endings at any stage were common and openly discussed. The commentators treat this ayah as addressing a specific point in that sequence rather than as a general statement, and the surrounding surah supplies the wider concern with how people are treated in a parting.

keyTerms.note: From the verb to count, so the term names a number of intervals rather than a state. The ayah says the count does not apply here, which the commentators tie to the reason it exists at all.

A verb for giving something to be enjoyed for a period, used in the Quran of the provision made at a parting. It names material support rather than a gesture, and it comes first of the two instructions.
A noun for setting free, used of turning grazing animals loose. Its pairing here with a word meaning beautiful occurs twice in this surah and nowhere else in the Quran.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: A marriage was an agreement between two families with property moving in both directions, and an ending was a public financial event as much as a private one. Everyone in a small city knew the terms, and how a man parted from a household set his reputation with every other household he might later deal with. Partings were conducted in view of neighbours who would be counting.
studies.didYouKnow: The phrase for a gracious release occurs twice in the whole Quran, and both occurrences are in this surah. The first is in the offer made to the Prophet's own household some twenty ayat earlier. The classical commentators connect the two, noting that the same wording is used for a household under revelation and for any household at all.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The passage separates what is required from what is fitting and then declines to let the second collapse into the first. A reader who learns that an obligation does not apply might reasonably conclude that nothing further is asked; the ayah answers that conclusion in the same sentence. That establishes a pattern in how the Quran handles reductions of burden, which is that the character of the person is addressed after the requirement is settled.

crossReferences.why: Treats the same case and names provision according to means, calling it a duty of the conscientious.
Uses the identical phrase for a gracious release, in the offer made to the household.
Adds that forgoing what one is owed in such a parting is nearer to mindfulness of God.

studies.applyIt: Think of an arrangement you are ending or have recently ended, at work or with a friend. Ask what is actually required of you, and then ask separately what would be gracious. This ayah puts those two questions in one sentence and does not let the first answer the second. Do the gracious thing once this week, in the smallest available form.

studies.title: A Provision Made For One Household
studies.meaning: The longest ayah of the surah sets out what was permitted to the Prophet in his own household, listing categories in careful order and marking one of them as belonging to him alone and not to the believers. Two clauses do the interpretive work. God says He already knows what has been laid down for everyone else, so the general arrangement is not being altered. And a purpose is stated at the end: that no constriction should fall on him. The passage is about one house.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, in the sequence dealing with the household of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The categories listed reflect the marriage practice of that society, in which kin on both sides were the ordinary field of a match and a settlement was paid at the making of one. The commentators treat the passage as descriptive of a particular case, and discuss the general arrangements in their comments on other passages entirely.

keyTerms.note: The plural of a word meaning a wage or a recompense, used across the Quran for the payment made in marriage. Its ordinary commercial sense marks the settlement as a real transfer rather than a token.

The verb for leaving one place for another under pressure, the word that names the community's own founding move. Attaching it to the list ties the categories to a shared history rather than to lineage alone.
From a root meaning unmixed, used of gold with nothing else in it. It marks one clause of the ayah as belonging to a single case and closes it off from the general provision immediately.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Cousins on both the father's and the mother's side were the expected field for a marriage in Arabia, and families kept the ties inside a known circle. Naming those four groups in order was the ordinary way of describing a kinship map, the same list a man would recite if asked about his relations. The ayah uses the plainest social vocabulary available to it.
studies.didYouKnow: This is the longest ayah in the surah by a clear margin, and it is one of very few in the Quran that mark something as applying to a single person rather than to everyone. The classical commentators discuss the exclusivity clause at length precisely because such marking is rare, and they read it as limiting rather than extending what the passage establishes.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The ayah distinguishes a general provision from a particular one and says so inside the text rather than leaving it to be inferred. That is a significant piece of self-interpretation: the Quran here marks a boundary around one of its own passages. It also states a reason, the removal of constriction, so the arrangement is presented as easing a difficulty in a specific life rather than as conferring a privilege.

crossReferences.why: Closes the same subject two ayat later by ruling out any further additions to the household.
Uses the same word for the marriage settlement in the general arrangement for everyone.
States the same purpose, the removal of a constriction, in the case that precedes this one.

studies.applyIt: Notice how carefully this ayah marks off what applies to one person from what applies to everyone. That distinction is easy to lose. When you next take a lesson from someone else's life, at work or in your family, ask which part of their situation was theirs alone. Most bad advice comes from skipping that question rather than from bad intentions.

studies.title: God Knows What Is In Hearts
studies.meaning: A latitude is described in the ordering of a household's arrangements, and then a reason is given for it that is entirely about other people's inner lives. The stated aim is threefold: that their eyes be cooled, that they not grieve, and that each be content with what she is given. The last clause turns the ayah around, saying God knows what is in your hearts, and the plural pronoun there includes everyone. The latitude and the scrutiny arrive together.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, in the sequence about the household. The commentators report differing accounts of how the latitude described here was actually used, and several note reports that the arrangements continued in a settled pattern afterwards. The reports differ, and the classical sources record the difference rather than resolving it. The ayah itself supplies only the permission and the reason attached to it.

keyTerms.note: A verb for putting something back in time rather than setting it aside. The same root gives the word for hope, since what is deferred is by definition still expected.

An Arabic idiom for settled contentment. Its literal sense is a coolness in the eye, understood against a climate where tears were hot and rest was what stopped them, so it names relief rather than delight.
A name for one who holds back from responding though fully able to. Paired here with knowing, it says the knowledge of what is in a heart is not immediately followed by consequence.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: A household of several dwellings ran on visible turns. Everyone knew whose day it was, and adjustments were noticed by neighbours as well as by those inside. In a settlement where courtyards adjoined, domestic arrangements were semi-public information and were read as statements about standing. That is the setting in which an ayah about deferring and receiving becomes a matter needing an explicit reason.
studies.didYouKnow: The idiom about a coolness in the eyes appears several times in the Quran and always describes relief from anxiety rather than pleasure. It is used of a mother given her child back, and of a request for family who bring peace of mind. The classical lexicographers explain the image from the heat of weeping, so a cool eye is one that has stopped.
studies.theologicalSignificance: A permission is granted and then immediately placed under observation, which is how the Quran often handles latitude. The reason offered is not the convenience of the one permitted but the settled state of the people affected, so even a discretion is described as being for somebody else's sake. And the forbearing name at the close says the knowledge of hearts does not function as a threat, which is what makes the scrutiny bearable.

crossReferences.why: Uses the same idiom of a mother whose child was returned to her, so she would not grieve.
Puts the same phrase in a prayer, asking for family who bring rest to the eyes.
Also pairs what hearts have earned with the name of God who is forbearing.

studies.applyIt: The reason given here is somebody else's peace of mind, not the convenience of the person with the discretion. Take one decision this week that is genuinely yours to make and ask what version of it would let the other people involved stop worrying. Then make that version. It is often only slightly different and it is almost never the default.

studies.title: No Exchange After This
studies.meaning: A door is closed. No further additions to the household, and no substitution of one for another, and the ayah says this holds even if beauty should attract. The commentators read the closing as arriving after the choice the household had already made, so what looks like a restriction functions as a settlement in their favour. The final name for God is one that occurs rarely, meaning the watchful observer, and it attaches to a passage about something nobody else could have enforced.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, following the ayat that describe the household's arrangements. The classical commentators connect this restriction to the offer put earlier in the surah, in which each member of the household was given a genuine choice and answered it. On that reading the closing of the door is the counterpart to what they accepted, and reports differ over the exact sequence without differing on the connection.

keyTerms.note: A verb for substituting one thing for another, used of trading goods. Its plainness is deliberate here, since what the ayah rules out is precisely the treating of people as interchangeable.

keyTerms.gloss: it pleases you, it strikes you
keyTerms.note: A verb for something catching the attention and impressing itself, from the root for wonder. It names an involuntary response rather than a choice, which is why the ayah can concede it and still close the door.
One who keeps something under continuous observation, from a root also used of a guard posted on high ground. The name appears five times in the Quran and always where something private is at issue.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Households of standing in Arabia were expected to grow. Alliances were made by marriage, and a man's connections were read from the families he had joined himself to, so closing off further additions cut a leader off from an ordinary instrument of politics. Everyone would have understood what was being given up, and the ayah names it without softening the cost in either direction.
studies.didYouKnow: The name of God that closes this ayah occurs five times in the Quran, and in every case it appears where something hidden or domestic is under discussion: the treatment of relatives, the private testimony of a prophet about his people, the recording of a word before it is spoken. The classical commentators note this consistency of placement.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The ayah concedes an inclination and then declines to give it any authority, which is a precise piece of moral description. Attraction is not denied, argued with, or condemned; it is simply not permitted to reopen a settled matter. That distinction between what a person feels and what a person may act on runs through the Quran's treatment of the inner life, and it is stated here in one clause.

crossReferences.why: Gives the choice this restriction answers, and what was accepted when it was offered.
Uses the same name for God, of an observer present for every word spoken.
Attaches the same name to the ties of kinship and the duty owed within them.

studies.applyIt: Notice how this ayah handles an attraction: it names it accurately and gives it no vote. Most of us do the opposite, either denying the feeling or treating it as information about what we should do. Pick one thing you want this week that you are not going to act on. Say both halves to yourself plainly, and leave them both standing.

studies.title: When You Have Eaten, Disperse
studies.meaning: The longest passage in the surah addresses a very ordinary problem: guests who arrive early and stay late. Entry by invitation, no waiting about for the food, no settling in for conversation afterwards. The reason given is startlingly plain, that this was wearing on the Prophet and he was too diffident to say so, and the ayah adds that God is not diffident about the truth. A screen is then named for the passing of things between rooms, with a reason attached about hearts on both sides.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan. The Prophet's dwellings opened directly onto the place of prayer and the household had almost no separation from public life; people came and went all day. The commentators report that the passage followed a gathering after a wedding meal at which guests lingered. The reports agree on the general setting and differ in their details, and the ayah itself names the difficulty it is addressing.

keyTerms.note: A verb for scattering outward, used of people spreading through a land and of things being spread out. Its ordinary, undramatic sense is the point: it simply asks guests to go home.

From the root for human company and familiarity, so it describes the pleasant sinking into conversation among friends. The word contains no criticism, which is what makes the instruction gentle rather than harsh.
The word for something dividing two spaces, a curtain or a wall. It occurs seven times in the Quran and never means a garment; here it names a physical divider inside a house.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Hospitality in Arabia had no clock. A guest was fed and then sat, and leaving early could be read as a slight to the host, so gatherings ran long by design. Houses were small, one or two rooms opening on a courtyard, and a household had nowhere to withdraw to while visitors remained. The problem the ayah names was structural rather than a matter of anyone's rudeness.
studies.didYouKnow: The word rendered as a screen occurs seven times in the Quran, and in every other place it names something that divides two spaces: a barrier between two groups on the Day of Judgement, a partition a woman withdrew behind, the veil through which God speaks to a human being. It never once refers to an article of clothing.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The passage says God is not diffident about the truth, and then demonstrates it by putting a small domestic irritation into scripture. That is a remarkable thing for a revealed text to spend its length on, and it establishes something about scale: the tiredness of one man in his own house is treated as worth addressing. Consideration is described here as a matter for revelation rather than merely for manners.

crossReferences.why: Gives the general rule for entering any house, including going away if asked to.
Addresses another matter of bearing towards the Prophet, about voices raised in his presence.
Uses the same word for a partition, there of how God speaks to a human being.

studies.applyIt: Somebody in your life is too polite to tell you that something you do is tiring. Think for a minute about who that is likely to be and what the thing is likely to be. You will usually already know. Ask them once this week, plainly, and make it easy to answer. This whole passage exists because that question was never asked.

studies.title: Whether You Reveal Or Hide
studies.meaning: A single general line follows the household instructions: whether you bring a thing out or keep it in, God knows everything. Then the next ayah lists the relations before whom no restriction applies at all, and closes by asking for mindfulness and naming God a witness. The commentators read the pair as a hinge. The first extends the matter inward, past anything anyone could enforce, and the second immediately marks out the ground where it does not apply.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, directly after the passage about entering the household and about the screen between rooms. The list in the second ayah answers the obvious question the first instruction raises: a rule about visitors is not a rule about family, and the categories are named rather than left to inference. The commentators treat it as clarification issued alongside the instruction rather than as a separate ruling.

keyTerms.note: A verb for making something appear, from the root that also gives the word for open country. Paired with concealment it covers the whole range of what a person can do with a thought.
From the root for a wing, so its underlying sense is a tilt away from straight. The Quran uses it mostly for the lifting of a restriction rather than for guilt actually incurred.
From the vocabulary of testimony, meaning one who was there and can speak to it. Closing a list of who may be present with a name meaning the one present is a deliberate turn.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: A house in that city was busy and shared. Fathers, brothers, nephews and household workers moved through it in the course of an ordinary day, and family business could not have been conducted any other way. Any instruction about visitors immediately raised the question of where the boundary fell. The list here reads like the answer given when somebody asks a practical question in a doorway.
studies.didYouKnow: The list of relations in the second ayah closely parallels one given in another Medinan surah, in nearly the same order. The two lists differ in a small number of items, and the classical commentators discuss those differences carefully, since each passage is answering a slightly different question about a slightly different situation.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Placing an ayah about God's knowledge between two practical instructions changes the register of both. Rules about doorways are put under an observation that reaches inside whoever is following them, which makes compliance a matter of intention rather than of appearance. And the exemption that follows shows the scrutiny is not an extension of the rule but a limit on how much rule was needed in the first place.

crossReferences.why: Gives a closely parallel list of relations, differing in a small number of items.
Says God will call to account for what is in the self, whether disclosed or concealed.
States that God knows what is in the breasts, whether you hide it or show it.

studies.applyIt: Take one thing you did this week that looked entirely correct from outside, and ask honestly what it was for. Not in order to convict yourself of anything. This ayah drops a statement about God's knowledge into the middle of some very ordinary etiquette, which suggests those two things belong together more often than we notice.

studies.title: God And His Angels Do This
studies.meaning: Something is stated before anything is asked. God and His angels do this, and only then are the believers told to join in. The commentators note that the single verb carries a different sense for each subject: from God it is mercy and honour extended, from the angels it is the asking for that, and from human beings it is a request made. So one word covers three actions, and what the community is invited into is already under way rather than being started by them.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan. The surah has been setting out how people should conduct themselves around the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)'s household, down to waiting for an invitation before entering and leaving once a meal is finished. This ayah sits inside that stretch and lifts the subject from courtesy at a doorway to a formula of honour. The sources report that the companions asked how the words should be said, and preserve accounts of the reply.

keyTerms.note: The verb behind the word for prayer, whose root sense is to incline toward or attend to. That one root can serve God, angels and people is why the classical explanation gives it three senses here.
From the root of soundness and safety. The greeting it names is a declaration that the other person is secure from you, which is why it doubles as the ordinary word for making peace.
The verbal noun repeating its own verb, a construction of emphasis. It asks for the greeting given properly and completely rather than muttered as a reflex in passing.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Forms of address were formal and public in Arabia. How a man was greeted on entering a gathering announced his standing, and poets were paid to compose praise for patrons that would be repeated at assemblies for years afterwards. A community that saw its messenger daily, sat with him and ate in his house, was here given a settled formula of honour for a person who was also a neighbour.
studies.didYouKnow: The same verb appears thirteen ayat earlier, at forty-three, where God and His angels are said to do this for the believers themselves, bringing them out of darkness into light. Within one surah the action runs in both directions: the community is told it is already receiving this, and is then asked to offer it toward the Prophet.
studies.theologicalSignificance: People are invited to take part in something described as already happening, which is an unusual structure for an instruction. It is not a duty to be discharged but a joining. The passage also places honour toward the messenger inside worship rather than beside it, while keeping the direction of the request unambiguous: what is being asked for is asked from God, and the asking is what human beings contribute.

crossReferences.why: Turns the same verb toward the believers, with the stated purpose of bringing them out of darkness.
Uses the same language of blessings and mercy descending, here upon those who hold under loss.
Shows the human form of the verb in use, a prayer offered over people as a settling for them.

studies.applyIt: The next time his name comes up, in a talk or a conversation or your own reading, say the words slowly instead of running them together under your breath. Once, deliberately, with the meaning of each half in mind. The ayah asks for the greeting given fully, and most of us long ago stopped hearing what we are saying.

studies.title: A Slander They Did Not Earn
studies.meaning: Two ayat, and the second carries the weight. The first names those who cause hurt to God and His Messenger and states what follows for them. The second turns to hurt done to ordinary believing men and women, and defines it with precision: for something they did not earn. What such people take up is named with two words, a falsehood that stuns and a plain wrongdoing. The commentators observe that the second ayah is longer and far more exact about the offence than the first.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan. The city had a standing problem with talk: rumour during the siege, false report afterwards, and accusations circulated about individuals. The commentators discuss several incidents in connection with these ayat and do not agree on which, if any, occasioned them. What they do agree on is the setting, a small community in which a story could reach every household inside a day.

keyTerms.note: The verb from the same root as the word for annoyance used earlier in the surah, so the harm named is social rather than physical. Applied to God, the commentators read it as opposition rather than injury.
From a root meaning to leave someone dumbfounded. It names not any lie but one so unexpected that the person accused is struck silent, which is exactly what a public accusation does.
A verb out of commerce, in the form that means deliberate acquisition. Used of deeds it makes the ayah exact: the wrong lies in the gap between what was said and what was actually earned.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: In a settlement of that size, reputation was a shared asset and a shared weapon. There were no records; a person was what people said about them, and a story once in circulation could not be recalled. Marriages, partnerships and protection all rested on standing, so an accusation was materially destructive as well as painful. The word chosen here for a slander is a word for something that lands like a blow.
studies.didYouKnow: The word for a stunning falsehood occurs four times in the Quran. Three of them fall in one earlier Medinan surah, applied to a withheld payment, to blaming an innocent person, and to what was said against Mary. This is the fourth. Because the word is rare, the classical commentators fix its sense here by reading those three alongside it.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The second ayah defines the wrong by a mismatch rather than by the content of the speech. What makes it slander is that the person did not earn it, so accuracy is the operative test and not the harshness of what was said. That carries an uncomfortable implication the passage does not pursue and does not hide: the same words about someone who had earned them would be a different question.

crossReferences.why: Uses the same word of one who commits a fault and then lays it on an innocent person.
Warns against suspicion and against speaking of a person who is not in the room.
Describes a rumour passed along as if it were slight, and calls it enormous instead.

studies.applyIt: You have almost certainly repeated something about someone this year without checking it. Take the one that comes to mind first. You do not need to trace it or confess it to anybody. Just decline to pass it on again, and if that person comes up in conversation this week, say the part you actually know and stop there.

studies.title: So They Would Be Recognised
studies.meaning: An instruction is given to be relayed, addressed to three groups in widening circles, from one household outward to the women of the community. What is asked concerns a garment already in ordinary use rather than a new one, and the verb describes how it is drawn rather than whether it is worn. A reason is then stated inside the ayah itself, which is unusual: so that they be recognised and not troubled. The commentators tie that reason to the conditions of the city and differ over its reach.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, at a period the classical sources describe as unsettled, with people troubled on the streets after dark by men who afterwards claimed not to have known whom they were addressing. The commentators connect the reason clause in the ayah to that situation. Reports differ over the particulars, and the sources describe the general conditions more consistently than they describe any single incident.

keyTerms.note: A verb for bringing something near rather than for putting it on. The garment is assumed to be worn already, and what the ayah describes is an adjustment in how it is drawn about a person.

A plural of a wide wrap worn over other clothing. The word occurs only here in the Quran, and the classical commentators describe the garment from the practice of their own regions rather than from the text.
A passive from the verb to know. The purpose named is that others identify them correctly, which places the reason in how a person is read by strangers rather than in the cloth itself.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: The city had no street lighting and nothing resembling a police force. Women went out after dark for necessities, often to the edges of the settlement, and the lanes between houses were unlit. Dress in that society signalled household and standing at a glance and was read that way by everyone. The reason stated in this ayah belongs to a place where being identifiable at night was a practical safeguard.
studies.didYouKnow: The word for the outer garment named here occurs only once in the whole Quran. The classical commentators describe it from the clothing of their own time and region, which differed from place to place, and they record the variation rather than settling it. Because the text supplies no description, the discussion has always rested on usage rather than on definition.
studies.theologicalSignificance: This is one of a small number of ayat that state their own purpose. That gives later readers something to reason with rather than an instruction standing alone, and the classical tradition has taken the stated reason seriously in its discussions. The widening of the address also matters: what is said first to one household is extended to a whole community inside the same sentence, without any change of tone.

crossReferences.why: Addresses a related matter for believing women and attaches its own reason to it.
Belongs to the same run of passages and likewise states the reason for what it asks.
Names clothing as a provision sent down, then calls the garment of mindfulness the better one.

studies.applyIt: Notice that this ayah supplies its own reason, which scripture does not always do. When you keep a practice you inherited, try naming the reason the text gives for itself before reaching for the reasons you were taught. Do that once this week with something you already do. Knowing what a thing is for usually changes how it is carried.

studies.title: If They Do Not Desist
studies.meaning: The whole ayah hangs on a condition, and the condition is a chance to stop. Three groups are named, the last of them by a word that occurs nowhere else in the Quran and means those who shake a place with alarming reports. What is threatened is not punishment in the abstract but the end of neighbourhood: they will not remain your neighbours except briefly. The commentators note that nothing follows automatically, since the ayah is built so that desisting closes it.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, in the closing movement of the surah. The city had been through a siege and its aftermath, and the classical sources describe a persistent problem of false reports circulating and of individuals troubling people in the streets. The commentators connect this ayah to that unrest rather than to a single incident, and the three groups it names correspond to the ones the surah has described at length.

keyTerms.note: A verb for reaching a limit and going no further, from the root that gives the word for a boundary. It makes the whole ayah conditional on a choice that remains available while it is being read.
From a verb for shaking or making tremble, used of the ground quaking. It names people who destabilise by report rather than by act, and it occurs only here in the whole Quran.
A verb for living alongside, from the word for a neighbour, which in Arabia also meant a person under one's protection. Losing that relation meant losing a claim as much as an address.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Neighbourhood in that society was a formal category. A neighbour had claims on you and you on him, and a man who granted protection to someone was said to have made him a neighbour. Poets boasted about how they treated theirs. To be told that a person would no longer be your neighbour was to be told about the withdrawal of a bond, not just about a change of house.
studies.didYouKnow: The word for those who spread alarming reports appears only once in the entire Quran, in this ayah. It is built from the verb used elsewhere of the earth quaking, so the image behind it is of ground shaking under people rather than of speech. The classical commentators explain it from that root, since the text gives them no second occurrence.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Placing everything under a condition changes what the ayah is doing. A warning that can be closed by stopping is an invitation as much as a threat, and the classical commentators read it that way. Naming the harm as unsettling speech also identifies something that a community can suffer without anyone striking a blow, and treats it as serious in proportion to its actual effect.

crossReferences.why: Uses the same verb for desisting and says what is past would then be forgiven them.
Describes reports about safety or alarm being broadcast rather than referred to those who could judge.
Warns those who like indecency to circulate among the believers, in a similar setting.

studies.applyIt: Notice how much of what you pass on is not information but atmosphere: a mood about how bad things are getting, shared without any fact attached. This ayah has a word for exactly that. Go one day without contributing to it in a group chat or at a table, and see how much of your usual talk it accounted for.

studies.title: No Change In God's Way
studies.meaning: A severe consequence is stated for the condition set out in the ayah before, and then the second ayah does something that changes how the first is read. It calls this God's established way with those who went before, and says no substitution will be found for it. The commentators understand the passage as describing what befell people who persisted in armed sedition against a community, in line with earlier precedents, and they treat it as the description of a consequence rather than as a standing instruction.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, in a city that had recently been besieged and was still unsettled. The commentators read these ayat with the previous one, which offers the alternative of desisting, and they discuss them in the context of a state at war rather than as general guidance. The classical literature treats the historical situation as essential to the passage rather than incidental to it.

keyTerms.note: A verb for encountering or overtaking someone, with a sense of finding after searching. It belongs to the vocabulary of a conflict already under way rather than to any settled procedure.
The word for a path worn by repeated use, so a settled practice. Attributed to God it names consistency across time, and the second ayah cites it as the reason the first should not surprise anyone.
A noun for exchanging one thing for another. Its indefinite form after a negation makes the denial total: not merely that no change has occurred, but that none is to be found at all.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: A city under threat had no institutions of the kind a modern reader assumes. There was no standing court, no prison and no police, and a settlement's safety rested on its ability to answer a danger directly. Sedition from inside during a siege was the gravest thing a community faced, because it opened the one approach that could not be defended. That is the situation the classical commentators keep in view.
studies.didYouKnow: The phrase for God's established way occurs twice in this surah, here and some twenty ayat earlier, where it was used to say that no difficulty attached to a prophet in what God ordained. The same term is applied in one place to a mercy and in the other to a consequence, which is how the classical commentators describe its neutrality.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Anchoring a present event in an old pattern does two things. It removes the sense that anything unprecedented is happening, which is the surah's habit throughout. And it places the outcome outside anyone's discretion by attributing it to a consistency older than the situation. The passage is hard, and the tradition has read it as bound to its circumstances rather than as a general licence, which is how it is presented here.

crossReferences.why: Sets the condition this passage answers, and offers desisting as the way it closes.
Uses the same phrase and adds that no turning aside will be found in God's way.
States the same principle of an unchanging pattern, in a passage about restraint from fighting.

studies.applyIt: This is among the hardest passages in the surah, and the honest thing is to read it slowly with its circumstances in view rather than to lift a clause out of it. When you next meet a difficult line in any text, resist quoting it before you have read what stands immediately before and after. Here, what stands before is an offer to stop.

studies.theme: Time and the Brevity of Life
studies.title: Perhaps The Hour Is Near
studies.meaning: A question is reported, an answer is given, and then the answer turns on the one giving it. The knowledge rests with God, and the next clause asks what the Prophet himself could know about it. The commentators note that the ayah refuses the question twice over, first by locating the knowledge elsewhere and then by including the messenger in the ignorance. What is offered instead is a possibility, phrased with a particle that leaves it genuinely open.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, though the question it reports had been put since the Meccan years. Commentators describe the asking as coming from more than one direction: some pressed it as a challenge and some out of genuine concern. The Quran gives the same answer in every period, which the classical sources treat as significant in itself, since the answer never develops or becomes more specific over twenty years.

keyTerms.note: The ordinary word for a portion of time, made definite. Using so plain a term for the end keeps it from becoming a title, and the article does all the work of identifying which hour is meant.
A verb of coming to know by reaching or catching up with something. In a question of this form the Quran uses it to say that the addressee has no access, and the addressee here is the Prophet.
A particle of expectation that never asserts. It leaves the nearness a live possibility rather than a prediction, which is precisely what makes the ayah an answer without being information.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Time in that society was kept by things that recur: the moon, the seasons of the caravan, the date harvest, the years named after events people remembered. There was no calendar of the kind that lets a person mark a distant date and count towards it. A question about when something would happen was normally answered by naming a season, and this question could not be answered at all.
studies.didYouKnow: The Quran reports this question being asked repeatedly, in Meccan and Medinan surahs alike, and the answer never varies in substance across all of them: the knowledge is with God. In one place the messenger is told to say it lies with his Lord alone and that its weight is heavy in the heavens and the earth. The refusal is consistent over the whole period of revelation.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The ayah establishes a limit inside prophecy itself. A messenger is not described as knowing everything he transmits from, and the text says so plainly rather than leaving the boundary vague. Replacing the date with a possibility also does something practical: a fixed date would let a person plan around it, and an open nearness cannot be planned around at all, which is the effect the passage is after.

crossReferences.why: Reports the same question and says its weight is heavy in the heavens and the earth.
Asks what the messenger has to do with mentioning it, and returns the matter to God.
Lists the knowledge of that hour among the things kept with God alone.

studies.applyIt: Notice that this ayah replaces a date with a possibility, and that the possibility is harder to live with than either certainty would be. Pick one thing you are putting off until you know more about the timing. Do the first small piece of it this week while the timing is still unknown. That is the whole practical content of the answer given here.

studies.title: If Only We Had Obeyed
studies.meaning: Three short ayat move from a statement to a scene. What is prepared is named, then the duration, then the absence of anyone to turn to, and only after all three does a voice appear. What it says is a wish rather than a plea, and it names two obediences that were not given. The commentators note that no argument is made at this point and no request either. The passage stops at the sentence, and the sentence is regret in its plainest available form.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, in the closing sequence of the surah. The surah has spent much of its length describing people who heard instructions and worked around them, during a siege and afterwards. These ayat give the far end of that behaviour, and the commentators read them as the counterpart to the earlier scenes rather than as a separate subject introduced at the close.

keyTerms.note: From a verb for kindling and for flames catching hold. The word occurs sixteen times across the Quran, and in this surah it appears only here, at the point where the consequence is first named.
A passive intensive from the verb to turn something around, built on the same root as the word for a heart. It describes faces being turned repeatedly rather than once.
A particle of wishing for what cannot be, attached to a pronoun. Arabic reserves it for the impossible, so the grammar of the sentence already contains the answer to what is being wished.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Regret in an oral society had a specific shape. There was no record to consult and no way to revisit what had been said, so a person carried their own account of a decision and could not check it. What was left when something went wrong was the memory of advice given and ignored, often by someone who had said it plainly at the time. The wish in this passage is that memory, spoken aloud.
studies.didYouKnow: The phrase used here for finding neither protector nor helper occurs six times in the Quran, and two of those are in this surah. The first came in the middle of the siege, where the same words were used of people looking for someone to shield them in this life. The surah closes the circle by using them again of a place where nobody is looking any more.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The order of the three ayat is doing the argument.
